matrix_note: Upstream LifeOS releases against a bare control. The private fork lane was retired after Phase 3: it required withheld transcripts, and the question worth publishing is whether the framework helps, not whose fork is better.

versions.note: Bare Claude Code, empty CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Control baseline: structurally cannot know the persona, so T5 grounding checks are skipped and it anchors the floor.
v5.0.0 ships a whole .claude tree with identity @-imports already ACTIVE and mode templates inline in CLAUDE.md.
v6.0.5 still has three modes, but defines them ONLY in LIFEOS_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md — which is why loading it via --append-system-prompt-file is mandatory, not optional.
v7.28.3 retired modes outright ('One format, every response — there are no modes'). Banner markers are null by fact, not by omission; routing is measured behaviourally via code:algorithm_read.

tier_models_note: T5 (personalization) runs on the two bisect models only. Grounding is a property of the scaffold, not of model tier, so paying for it across eight models buys little.

runner.isolation: HOME redirected to sandboxes/_home/<VERSION> (fidelity) + sandbox-exec seatbelt denying the operator home (safety) + LeakCheck marking escapes contaminated (validity)

claudex.note: GPT through the SAME CC harness via claudex (ChatGPT-auth wrapper) so hooks fire identically — this isolates prompts-vs-plumbing.
